content.title: Suns vs. Timberwolves: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/17)
content.text: The Phoenix Suns (39–29) visit the Minnesota Timberwolves (41–27) tonight at the Target Center in Minneapolis in a matchup with major playoff implications. The Suns have dropped two straight after a four-game winning streak. They fell to the Toronto Raptors on Friday, 122–115, and then to the Boston Celtics last night, 120–112, despite strong scoring performances from Devin Booker and Jalen Green. Booker poured in 41 points in Monday’s loss to Boston, while Green scored 34 against Toronto. With Dillon Brooks out, Phoenix has a new scoring tandem, with Booker averaging 30.9 PPG this month, with Green close behind at 24.6 PPG. But the supporting cast has struggled to produce. Collin Gillespie has scored just three total points over the past two games, shooting 1-for-11 during that stretch. Phoenix’s typically solid defense has also faltered against two balanced opponents. The Suns sit seventh in the Western Conference, currently positioned for a play-in tournament spot but just two games behind the Timberwolves for the final automatic playoff berth. With Anthony Edwards sidelined for Minnesota due to knee inflammation — an injury expected to keep him out for one to two weeks — Phoenix has an opportunity to gain ground in the standings with a win tonight and continued momentum in the coming games. Edwards scored 19 points in Minnesota’s 116–103 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday, shooting 6-of-17 as the knee issue appeared to limit his effectiveness. Julius Randle led the Timberwolves with 32 points on 11-of-18 shooting, snapping a five-game stretch in which he had failed to reach 20. Prior to Sunday, Randle had averaged just 13.7 points per game over his previous 11 outings. Minnesota will need him to sustain that scoring level in the coming weeks to avoid slipping into play-in tournament territory. With Edwards out and Phoenix holding the edge in late-game shot creation behind Booker and Green, expect the Suns to pull away late. Prediction: Phoenix Suns 120, Minnesota Timberwolves 113 Injury Report Phoenix Suns Haywood Highsmith — GTD (Knee) Grayson Allen — GTD (Knee) Dillon Brooks — Out (Hand) Mark Williams — Out (Foot) Minnesota Timberwolves Anthony Edwards — Out (Knee) How to Watch Suns vs. Timberwolves Tip-off for tonight’s Suns-Timberwolves game is set for 8:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Central / 5:00 PM Mountain at the Target Center in Minneapolis.
